title: Reseat a board that missed one of its two supports, without knocking over the bottle beside it
instruction: Set the board across both wooden blocks without toppling a block, dropping the board or knocking the bottle over.
context: A shelf or board that misses one of its supports is a common slip when setting up at home or in a workshop. The fix is to lift it clear and seat it again, without swinging it into whatever stands next to it, here a glass bottle that would fall and break.
setup: Coordinates in cm on the table top: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left from the midline between them. Two loose pine blocks, each 8 (x) by 4 (y) by 8 cm tall, 200 g, stand upright centred at x 30, y +17 and y -17, so their inner faces are 30 cm apart. A pine board 40 cm long, 5 cm wide, 2 cm thick, 250 g, lies along y at x 30: it was set down 6 cm too far left, so it rests on the inner top edge of the left block and slopes about 16 degrees down to the right, its centre at y +5.6 and its right end on the table at about y -13.6, 3 cm short of the right block; its left end overhangs the left block's outer face by about 6 cm. The hazard: an empty brown glass beer bottle (6 cm across, 22.2 cm tall, 200 g) stands upright at x 40, y -12, 4.5 cm behind the board's back edge, beside its low end. Distractors further back, which scoring ignores: a red ceramic mug (9 cm across, 8 cm tall, 11.4 cm with its handle, 300 g) at x 46, y +22, handle toward the robot; a roll of clear packing tape (10 cm across, 5 cm tall, 60 g) lying flat at x 48, y -25; a Phillips PH2 screwdriver (18.8 cm long, 100 g) lying parallel to the board, centred at x 44, y +3.4. Both grippers start open at the ready pose. One fixed layout, shown in the screenshot.
scoring: Checked 20 times a second. The score is 0 for the rest of the trial, whatever happens afterwards, if at any point a block tilts more than 20 degrees, the whole board lies on the table (its top less than 4 cm above the table), or the bottle tilts more than 20 degrees or its base moves more than 2 cm. Otherwise, at the end: the board counts as seated when it is at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), level within 3 degrees, its underside within 1 cm of the top of each block, each end within 3 cm of its block's centre front to back and at least 0.5 cm over its block along the board, and both blocks stand upright within 5 degrees. 1.0 when it is seated with at least 3 cm of each end over its block and neither block moved more than 2 cm; 0.5 when it is seated but an end has less than 3 cm over its block or a block moved 2 to 5 cm; 0 otherwise, including a block moved more than 5 cm. A full score that holds for 3 seconds ends the trial. Grippers may still touch the board at the end.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Mark the blocks' and the bottle's positions on the table, stand them on the marks, and lay the board on the left block's inner edge with its centre 5.6 cm left of the midline so its right end drops to the table.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena (PhysX at 240 Hz, 20 Hz control) on a replica of a calibrated two-arm YAM station. The blocks and board are rigid boxes; every object has rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), above pine on pine (about 0.5). The bottle, mug, tape and screwdriver are NVIDIA SimReady models (CC-BY 4.0) with set masses; the bottle cannot break, so a knock is judged by its tilt and displacement. No force sensing. The board falls into its sloped start during a 0.5 s settle.
